title: This Diwali Muhurat, Let me Show you How To Build a Winning STOCK Portfolio! | Rahul Jain
creator: Rahul Jain
source_note: Detailed summary generated from the video's English auto-captions; a portfolio-construction tutorial, not a stock-picking video - all stocks named are explicitly random demonstration picks, not recommendations.
summary: Rahul Jain uses the Diwali Muhurat occasion to teach portfolio construction rather than stock picking, arguing that 'which stocks look attractive now?' is the wrong question after two flat years for Indian markets. His five-step framework starts with writing down the portfolio's goal, covering purpose (his example: a daughter's education), expected return (15-18% CAGR over 7 years) and maximum tolerable loss (15%), since the goal drives time frame, stock choice and exits. Step two is choosing a stock-selection strategy and universe, demonstrated on Smallcase: over five years only 11 of 100 large caps delivered negative CAGR (worst about -10%), versus 22 of 150 midcaps (worst -16%) and 88 of about 600 small/micro caps (worst -27%), so he maps cap segments to a 2x2 matrix of horizon (3-5 vs 5-20 years) against loss tolerance (up to 20% vs up to 40%). Step three sets rules: no sector above 20-25% and no single stock above 10% (his own rule). Step four benchmarks the portfolio (his demo beats its large/midcap benchmark since June 2026 but fell harder on 23 October); step five rebalances at portfolio level: trim winners that breach weight, exit losers rather than holding them in hope. The stocks named on screen (Tata Motors, Eicher Motors, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Zydus, HDFC Bank, SBI, LIC, Bajaj Finserv, Shriram Finance, Coal India, Bharat Coking Coal, NTPC) are explicitly random demonstration picks, not recommendations, so no calls are recorded. Auto-captions garble some names (e.g. 'Aishar Motors', 'Bajage Fininserve', 'LIIC', 'Vanta power').
